import unicodedata
from setuptools.command.egg_info import translate_pattern
nfc = unicodedata.normalize('NFC', 'café.txt')
nfd = unicodedata.normalize('NFD', 'café.txt')
assert nfc != nfd          # the two byte forms genuinely differ
m = translate_pattern(nfc).match(nfd)   # pattern composed, path decomposed
print('MATCH:', m is not None)
assert m is not None       # Fails at the parent commit: pattern does not match
PY
observed_failure_at_parent: 'MATCH: False' — translate_pattern() compiles the pattern byte-for-byte, so a MANIFEST.in exclude/global-exclude/recursive-exclude/prune rule authored in NFC does not match a file whose on-disk name is stored in NFD (the two forms differ byte-wise but denote the same file), and the excluded non-ASCII-named file silently leaks into the built source distribution.
verified: In bench-base:python-3.12: at parent 84ed5913 the repro printed 'MATCH: False', egg_info.py contained no _NormalizedMatcher (grep -c == 0) and unicode_utils.py had no normalize() (grep -c 'def normalize' == 0), and the fix-commit test file failed ('2 failed, 67 deselected': test_translate_pattern_unicode_normalization + test_global_exclude_unicode_normalization). At fix dd9f436a3 the repro printed 'MATCH: True', _NormalizedMatcher present (3 references), unicode_utils.normalize present, and `python -m pytest -q setuptools/tests/test_manifest.py -k unicode_normalization` -> '2 passed, 67 deselected'.
install_recipe: cd <repo> && git reset --hard <sha> && git config --global --add safe.directory <repo> && pip install -e '.[test]' && pip install coverage (pytest.ini filterwarnings references the coverage module; without it collection aborts with a config warning) && pip install 'pytest==8.4.2'. Golden tests: pytest -q setuptools/tests/test_manifest.py -k unicode_normalization
issue_paraphrase: When a project's MANIFEST.in uses exclude, global-exclude, recursive-exclude or prune rules on files with non-ASCII names, a file whose on-disk name differs from the rule's text only in Unicode normalization form is not excluded: the pattern and the path are compared byte-for-byte, and one form (e.g. composed, as most editors write) does not equal the other (e.g. decomposed, as macOS filesystems frequently store it). The file then still ships inside the built source distribution even though the author explicitly excluded it, so the archive contains files the manifest says must not be there.
fix_summary: FileList matching now normalizes both the compiled pattern and the candidate path to NFC before matching, via a new unicode_utils.normalize() helper and a _NormalizedMatcher wrapper returned by translate_pattern(), so exclusion rules apply regardless of which normalization form the pattern or the stored file name uses. (Security-hardening fix for advisory GHSA-h35f-9h28-mq5c.)

The bench-base:python-3.12 image ships no C compiler and no stdlib Lib/test; neither is needed for this entry (only for the archive_util entry). pytest==8.4.2 avoids the module-level PytestRemovedIn10Warning that aborts collection of some test modules under pytest 9.1.1 with the repo's 'error' warning filter. import io, tarfile, tempfile, os
from setuptools import archive_util
tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()
tgz = os.path.join(tmp, 'malicious.tar.gz')
with tarfile.open(tgz, mode='w:gz') as t:
    for name in ['..\\escaped.txt', 'inside.txt']:
        info = tarfile.TarInfo(name)
        data = name.encode(); info.size = len(data)
        t.addfile(info, io.BytesIO(data))
dest = os.path.join(tmp, 'dest')
archive_util.unpack_archive(tgz, dest)
names = sorted(os.path.relpath(os.path.join(r, f), dest) for r, d, fs in os.walk(dest) for f in fs)
print('EXTRACTED:', names)
assert names == ['inside.txt'], names   # Fails at the parent: '..\\escaped.txt' is also extracted
PY
observed_failure_at_parent: 'EXTRACTED: ['..\\escaped.txt', 'inside.txt']' — the traversal guard in archive_util split member names on '/' alone (`'..' in name.split('/')`), so a member named with a single backslash separator passed all checks and was written into the extraction directory (on Linux as a literal filename containing a backslash; on Windows the same name resolves to a path outside the extraction directory, so a crafted archive can plant files outside the target folder).

At fix 72974110e2 the repro printed 'EXTRACTED: ['inside.txt']', _resolve_dest present (12 references), and `python -m pytest -q setuptools/tests/test_archive_util.py` -> '14 passed, 1 xpassed'.
install_recipe: cd <repo> && git reset --hard <sha> && git config --global --add safe.directory <repo> && pip install -e '.[test]' && pip install 'pytest==8.4.2'. The image's python lacks the stdlib Lib/test package, which tests/test_archive_util.py needs via .compat.py39 -> jaraco.test.cpython.from_test_support('can_symlink') ('ModuleNotFoundError: No module named test' at collection); fix by copying CPython 3.12.13's Lib/test into /usr/local/lib/python3.12/test (verified) or by relying on the direct repro, which needs nothing. Apply a pip-installable workaround only if the direct repro is not used. Golden tests: pytest -q setuptools/tests/test_archive_util.py
issue_paraphrase: When an archive (tar or zip) is unpacked into a directory, member names that use a backslash instead of a slash — or that carry a drive letter or UNC prefix — slip past the path-traversal guard, because the guard only splits member names on '/' when looking for '..' components. On Windows such a member resolves outside the intended extraction directory, so a maliciously crafted archive can write files outside the target folder; on other platforms its name is extracted as a surprising literal file name containing backslashes. The fix makes both archive drivers reject these names and confirms the resolved destination really stays inside the extraction directory.
fix_summary: archive_util now funnels both the zip and tar extraction drivers through a single _resolve_dest() helper that rejects member names containing backslashes, drive letters or UNC prefixes and, as defense in depth, verifies (via commonpath) that the resolved destination still falls under the extraction directory; unsafe members are skipped while safe ones are still extracted. (Security fix for advisory GHSA-grgh-hr87-3jpw; a follow-up commit bebbe6b87e changes skipping into raising UnsafeMember.)

Needs the Lib/test stdlib extraction (remedy above) for the golden tests only. Both tar and zip drivers are covered by the parametrized golden tests. Verified under pytest 8.4.2 and 9.1.1.

print('safer_name(unicode.dist) =', safer_name('unicode.dist'))

issue_paraphrase: Wheels built for distributions whose names contain dots, upper-case letters, or runs of punctuation get a wheel file name that keeps those characters verbatim (e.g. 'unicode.dist-0.1-py3-none-any.whl' for the distribution 'unicode.dist') instead of the canonical lowercased, separator-collapsed form ('unicode_dist-0.1-...') required by the wheel/binary-distribution specification, and the wheel's internal .dist-info directory name has the same problem. Tools that derive the project name from the wheel file name, or expect the .dist-info directory to match the normalized project name, then fail to recognize or process the wheel correctly.
fix_summary: safer_name() (the function that produces the distribution component of wheel filenames and dist-info directory names) now implements the spec's name normalization: collapse runs of [-_.] into '-', lowercase, then replace '-' with '_'. The duplicated private safer_name/safe_name in bdist_wheel.py were removed so the command uses the shared _normalization helper. Fixes issue #3777 via PR #4766.

    d = Distribution({'name': 'foo', 'version': ver})
    print('get_fullname(version=%s) ->' % ver, d.get_fullname())

issue_paraphrase: The names of the artifacts setuptools produces — source-distribution archives and the .egg-info directory component derived from the project's full name — lose version information: the version is rewritten into a canonicalized shorthand before being put into the file name, so a project that declares version '1.0' gets archives named with '1', and a project with no explicit version (default '0.0.0') gets archives named with '0'. The file names then disagree with the full version string recorded inside the metadata, which breaks release tooling, artifact matching and users reading the artifacts.
fix_summary: Distribution.get_fullname() (patched in from setuptools/_core_metadata.py) stopped running the version through packaging.utils.canonicalize_version and now embeds self.get_version() verbatim, so artifact names keep the user's version string exactly (the canonical_name part for the project name was already fine). Closes #4302 (and #3593).
